event_v0.doc: Deposit accepted. Carries the complete order so clients can recover the body\nthey must resupply for every later settlement call.
event_v0.name: Opened

params.doc: Commitment to the complete order, network, and this escrow; indexed topic.
params.name: order_id

params.doc: Complete canonical body required for every later settlement call.
params.name: order

function_v0.doc:
Deposit an order's inputs and return its domain-separated order ID.

# Authorization
`order.user` authorizes `(order_id,)` and the exact token-transfer subcalls.
Persist canonical order XDR before submission: only status is stored on-chain.

# Effects
Requires `now < fill_deadline <= expires`, 1\xe2\x80\x934 inputs/outputs, positive i128 input
amounts, unique output identities, local contract token/oracle addresses, and the
configured origin chain. Stores `Deposited`, renews data TTL, and emits `Opened`.
All transfers and writes roll back if any input fails to credit its exact amount.

# Errors
Admission/domain errors, `InvalidDeadlines`, `DuplicateOutput`, `InvalidInput`,
`InvalidStatus` for a retained order ID, and `ShortCredit`; token/auth failures
also abort. A nonce alone does not prevent opening a different complete order.
function_v0.name: open

event_v0.doc: Inputs returned to the recorded user, by expiry or by a proven non-fill.
event_v0.name: Refunded

params.doc: Refunded order commitment; indexed topic. The recorded user receives all inputs.
params.name: order_id

event_v0.doc: Inputs released to `destination` on behalf of the authorizing `claimant`.
event_v0.name: Finalised

params.doc: Authorized native identity committed by the first output solver.
params.name: claimant

params.doc: Native address receiving every escrowed input.
params.name: destination

function_v0.doc:
Return all inputs to the recorded user after `now > order.expires`.

Permissionless: only transaction fees need a payer; the payout address cannot be
changed. Resupply the exact order body. Transitions `Deposited` to `Refunded` and
emits `Refunded`; a token failure rolls back the entire call. Does not renew data TTL.

# Errors
`UnknownOrder`, `InvalidStatus`, or `DeadlineNotPassed`, plus token failures.
Deadline comparison uses the full u64 ledger time, including beyond the u32 wire range.
function_v0.name: refund

function_v0.doc:
Release all inputs to `destination` after every committed output is proven filled.

`solves` supplies one solver/timestamp per output in order; solvers may differ.
The first solver must equal the native `claimant` address commitment.

# Authorization
The claimant authorizes `(order_id, solves, claimant, destination)`; the actual
invocation still supplies the full original order. Each timestamp must be at or
before `fill_deadline`; the selected input oracle authenticates every proof.

# Effects
Transitions `Deposited` to `Claimed` before transfers and emits `Finalised`.
A failure rolls back the transition and all payouts. Data TTL is not renewed.
Claims remain available after expiry and can race a permissionless refund.

# Errors
`UnknownOrder`, `InvalidStatus`, `InvalidProofCount`, `ClaimantMismatch`,
`DeadlinePassed`, invalid addresses, or a downstream oracle/token/auth failure.
function_v0.name: finalise

function_v0.doc:
Renew an existing order entry, including terminal status, and instance/code TTL.

Permissionless; returns `true` if the entry exists and `false` for an unknown ID.
Uses the common capped renewal policy. Restore archived entries before invoking;
maintenance does not restore them. Configuration errors abort the call.
function_v0.name: maintain

function_v0.doc:
Read retained status, or `None` for an unknown order commitment.

Permissionless; maintains instance/code TTL but not the order entry. Numeric
states are `Deposited = 0`, `Claimed = 1`, `Refunded = 2`. Terminal states remain
as replay evidence. Archived state must be restored; it is not an unknown order.
Configuration errors or host archival failures abort the call.
function_v0.name: order_status

function_v0.doc:
Bind this deployment to its immutable OIF `chain_id` and Stellar `network_id`.

# Errors
Returns `WrongNetwork` unless `network_id` equals the host ledger network ID.
Stores configuration in instance storage and maintains instance/code TTL.
No administrator or subsequent configuration entrypoint exists.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Return the order commitment for this network and escrow without depositing funds.

The preimage is `"OIF.Stellar.Order.v1" || network[32] || escrow[32] || Order.to_xdr()`.
Checks bounded nonempty collections and output byte lengths; it does not perform
all `open` admission checks. No user authorization is required. Maintains instance/code TTL.

# Errors
`EmptyCollection`, `ResourceLimit`, or configuration errors.
function_v0.name: order_identifier

function_v0.doc:
Open `order`, pay its inputs to `destination`, run the solver hook, then require fills.

Mirrors EVM `openForAndFinalise`: the solver may fund outputs from the inputs it
just received. When `call` is nonempty, `destination` must be a contract
implementing `InputCallback::order_finalised(inputs, call)`; inputs are passed
unmodified. Every output is then checked against the input oracle with
`Solve { solver: commitment(claimant), timestamp: now }`. There is no same-chain
restriction; the oracle check is the only gate. Soroban forbids re-entry, so
`destination` must not be this escrow or the invoking contract, and nested atomic
opens on the same escrow are impossible.

# Authorization
`order.user` authorizes `(order_id,)` and the token subcalls, as for `open`;
`claimant` authorizes `(order_id, claimant, destination, call)`.

# Effects
Emits `Opened` then `Finalised`; ends `Claimed`. Any failure, including an
unproven output, rolls back the whole invocation.

# Errors
`open` admission errors, `AddressType`, `Unpr
function_v0.name: open_and_finalise

function_v0.doc:
Return inputs to the recorded user when one committed output is proven unfilled.

`output_index` is zero-based. Requires `now > order.fill_deadline` and a proof
reconstructed with the original deadline and output domain, not a caller-chosen
replacement. No user authorization is required; resupply the exact order body.
Transitions `Deposited` to `Refunded` and emits `Refunded`; token failures roll back
state and payouts. Does not renew data TTL.

# Errors
`UnknownOrder`, `InvalidStatus`, `DeadlineNotPassed`, `InvalidIndex`, or `Unproven`,
plus downstream oracle/token failures.
function_v0.name: refund_on_non_fill

udt_error_enum_v0.doc:
Settlement errors, codes 2000\xe2\x80\x932033, grouped by the phase that raises them.

Oracle adapters use 1000\xe2\x80\x931010 and the router adapter 3000\xe2\x80\x933009. All three ranges
avoid the Stellar Asset Contract's 1\xe2\x80\x9315 and the LI.FI router's codes below 1000:
nested failures propagate their callee's number, and a caller's typed client would
otherwise decode, say, a missing trustline as a settlement error.
udt_error_enum_v0.name: Error

cases.doc: Truncated, trailing, or otherwise malformed packed encoding.
cases.name: Malformed

cases.doc: Proof prefix does not identify a supported fill/non-fill encoding.
cases.name: UnknownDomain

cases.doc: A variable length or count cannot fit its u16 wire field.
cases.name: WireLimit

cases.doc: A collection or byte field exceeds the lower execution admission limit.
cases.name: ResourceLimit

cases.doc: An unsigned wire amount cannot fit a nonnegative native i128 token amount.
cases.name: AmountRange

cases.doc: Ledger time cannot be represented as a u32 wire timestamp.
cases.name: TimestampRange

cases.doc: Constructor `network_id` differs from the host ledger.
cases.name: WrongNetwork

cases.doc: An order or output does not name the configured local OIF chain.
cases.name: WrongChain

cases.doc: An output does not name this output-settler contract.
cases.name: WrongSettler

cases.doc: Address is not a supported G/C identity, or a contract address was required.
cases.name: AddressType

cases.doc: Local output execution was requested with nonempty callback data.
cases.name: CallbackUnsupported

cases.doc: Context kind or exact byte length is unsupported.
cases.name: InvalidContext

cases.doc: Before exclusivity ends, proposed solver differs from the exclusive claimant.
cases.name: Exclusive

cases.doc: The proposed origin solver identifier is all zero bytes.
cases.name: ZeroSolver

cases.doc: Checked U256 pricing arithmetic overflowed.
cases.name: Arithmetic

cases.doc: Fill time or supplied proof timestamp exceeds the allowed fill deadline.
cases.name: DeadlinePassed

cases.doc: A strictly-after deadline condition for non-fill/refund has not been met.
cases.name: DeadlineNotPassed

cases.doc: An existing fill blocks non-fill emission or wins first-output batch competition.
cases.name: AlreadyFilled

cases.doc: An order or fill batch is empty where at least one item is required.
cases.name: EmptyCollection

cases.doc: Two committed outputs have the same full packed-mandate identity.
cases.name: DuplicateOutput

cases.doc: Opening does not satisfy now < fill_deadline <= expires.
cases.name: InvalidDeadlines

cases.doc: Order ID is already retained, or settlement requires a deposited status.
cases.name: InvalidStatus

cases.doc: No retained status exists for the supplied complete order commitment.
cases.name: UnknownOrder

cases.doc: An input transfer did not increase escrow balance by exactly its amount.
cases.name: ShortCredit

cases.doc: Number of solves differs from committed outputs or no first solver exists.
cases.name: InvalidProofCount

cases.doc: Native claimant commitment differs from the first output solver.
cases.name: ClaimantMismatch

cases.doc: The selected oracle does not prove the requested non-fill.
cases.name: Unproven

cases.doc: Requested output index is outside the committed output vector.
cases.name: InvalidIndex

cases.doc: Required immutable deployment configuration is missing.
cases.name: NotConfigured

cases.doc: An input token amount is not strictly positive.
cases.name: InvalidInput

cases.doc: Output oracle is not this settler, so it cannot attest locally.
cases.name: WrongOracle

cases.doc: No stored fill record matches the supplied solver and timestamp.
cases.name: InvalidAttestation

cases.doc: Retaining the fill record until `fill_deadline + NOT_FILLED_WINDOW` would exceed\nthe host's maximum temporary-entry TTL; fill once the deadline is nearer.
cases.name: FillHorizon

cases.doc: Non-fill emission was requested after `fill_deadline + NOT_FILLED_WINDOW`.
cases.name: NotFilledWindowElapsed

udt_struct_v0.doc: One escrowed input. Inputs are always local, so `token` is the native contract\naddress the escrow calls directly; only outputs use raw wire identifiers.\n`amount` must convert to a positive `i128`.
udt_struct_v0.name: Input

fields.doc: Unsigned token base units; escrow requires 1 through i128::MAX and exact credit.
fields.name: amount

fields.doc: Native local token contract address, including the XLM SAC for native XLM.
fields.name: token

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A Stellar-origin order. Its opaque ID is the Keccak of a versioned domain, the
network ID, the escrow contract ID and this struct's canonical XDR, so every
field is committed and settlement calls must resupply the exact body.
`fill_deadline` bounds output fills and proof timestamps (inclusive);
`expires` is the earliest second after which an unconditional refund is allowed
(`now > expires`). Both are Unix seconds. `input_oracle` is the local contract
consulted for remote proofs; the user chooses and trusts it.
udt_struct_v0.name: Order

fields.doc: Permissionless expiry refunds start strictly after this absolute Unix second.
fields.name: expires

fields.doc: Inclusive latest valid fill timestamp in absolute Unix seconds.
fields.name: fill_deadline

fields.doc: User-selected local proof oracle; must be a C-contract and is a trust dependency.
fields.name: input_oracle

fields.doc: Ordered 1\xe2\x80\x934 local inputs; exact vector contents are part of the order ID.
fields.name: inputs

fields.doc: User-chosen bytes committed in this order; not a global nonce lock.
fields.name: nonce

fields.doc: OIF origin chain ID; must match input escrow configuration.
fields.name: origin_chain

fields.doc: Ordered 1\xe2\x80\x934 unique full mandates; the first output determines settlement ownership.
fields.name: outputs

fields.doc: Native depositor, authorizer and exclusive refund recipient.
fields.name: user

udt_struct_v0.doc: Who filled one output and when, as recorded on the output chain. `solver` is\nthe origin-side claimant identifier proposed at fill time, independent of the\naccount that paid the tokens; for a Stellar claimant it is an address commitment.
udt_struct_v0.name: Solve

fields.doc: Opaque origin claimant ID; Stellar claimants use typed native address commitments.
fields.name: solver

fields.doc: Source fill time in Unix seconds; must not exceed the committed fill deadline.
fields.name: timestamp

udt_enum_v0.doc: Persistent order state. The only transitions are `Deposited -> Claimed` and\n`Deposited -> Refunded`; terminal entries are retained as replay evidence.
udt_enum_v0.name: OrderStatus

cases.doc: Inputs are held and may be claimed or refunded according to the order.
cases.name: Deposited

cases.doc: Inputs were released to the authorized claimant destination; terminal replay evidence.
cases.name: Claimed

cases.doc: Inputs were returned to the recorded user; terminal replay evidence.
cases.name: Refunded

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The shared cross-chain output, field for field the reference `MandateOutput`.
Every field is a wire identifier, so `token`, `settler` and `oracle` are raw
32-byte IDs and `recipient` is a raw 32-byte payload rather than a native
`Address`: the output may live on any chain and is hashed into proofs as-is.
`amount` is the original mandate amount; Dutch pricing never changes it.
udt_struct_v0.name: MandateOutput

fields.doc: Original unsigned destination base-unit amount; context pricing does not alter the commitment.
fields.name: amount

fields.doc: Opaque destination callback bytes, at most 256; Stellar fills require empty bytes.
fields.name: callback_data

fields.doc: Full unsigned 256-bit OIF destination chain ID.
fields.name: chain_id

fields.doc: Opaque fulfillment context, at most 256 bytes; local execution uses supported exact layouts.
fields.name: context

fields.doc: Raw output-oracle ID; the source adapter must attest in this exact namespace.
fields.name: oracle

fields.doc: Destination recipient identifier; Stellar uses the raw G key or C ID typed by the context tag.
fields.name: recipient

fields.doc: Raw destination output-settler/application ID.
fields.name: settler

fields.doc: Destination token identifier; Stellar uses the raw SAC/C-contract ID.
fields.name: token
